analysis.investment_thesis: EID Parry is the closest among this group to meeting my quantitative entry criteria — P/E of 14.6x barely clears my 15x threshold and P/S of just 0.41x is genuinely attractive — but a P/B of 1.78x and the inherent cyclicality of sugar prevent a full endorsement. At a modest further price decline toward book value, this warrants serious re-examination.
key_strengths: P/E of 14.6x and EV/EBITDA of 5.92x are the lowest absolute valuations in this peer group — approaching Benjamin Graham territory
Debt-to-equity of 0.18 is conservative; borrowings were slashed from INR 4,347 Cr (2020) to INR 1,229 Cr (2021) and remain controlled
Ten consecutive years of positive net profit (INR 175 Cr at trough, INR 1,828 Cr at peak) demonstrating earnings durability across commodity cycles
key_risks: Sugar is a regulated, politically-sensitive commodity — government price controls and ethanol blending policy can compress margins overnight
Operating margin of only 6.12% provides a thin buffer; a modest revenue decline could eliminate profitability at the parent level
Cash has collapsed from INR 1,440 Cr (2023) to INR 404 Cr (2025) while capex accelerated to INR 1,046 Cr — rising capital intensity with higher borrowings
red_flags: P/B of 1.78x exceeds my preferred 1.5x ceiling — no margin of safety on an asset basis at current price
Free cash flow turned negative in FY23 (-INR 370 Cr) — commodity cycles can rapidly erode FCF
Other income surged to INR 706 Cr in FY25 (up from INR 304 Cr in FY24), inflating reported net profit; underlying operating earnings are more modest
analysis.detailed_analysis:
EID Parry, founded in 1788, passes my P/E test at 14.6x — the only stock in this set to do so. The P/S of 0.41x on INR 31,600 Cr of revenue and an EV/EBITDA of under 6x reflect genuine value characteristics in the headline numbers. The balance sheet improvement from 2020 to 2022 — when borrowings fell from INR 4,347 Cr to INR 1,259 Cr — was exemplary, and the company holds stakes in Coromandel International which provide hidden value.

However, I must not ignore the P/B of 1.78x (above my 1.5x maximum) and the thin 6.12% operating margin. The business earned only INR 175 Cr of net profit as recently as 2016, and the recent FY25 profit of INR 1,773 Cr is substantially inflated by INR 706 Cr of 'other income.' Stripping that out reveals a more modest core operation. I would require the stock to trade closer to 1.2–1.4x book before committing capital with a proper margin of safety.
